questions.title: Shape Area Override Drill
questions.description:
Core override drill: a child class replaces a parent method with its own version.

Output Format:

questions.title: Eq Override Point Match Drill
questions.description:
Magic method drill: __eq__ compares field values instead of object identity.
Chip stores coordinates x and y; __eq__ returns True when both fields match. Read two chips' coordinates and print the result of ==.

Input Format:
Line 1: x1 y1
Line 2: x2 y2

Output Format:
Print True if both coordinates match, otherwise False

Constraints:
-1000 <= x, y <= 1000
questions.sampleoutput1: True
questions.output1: True
questions.output3: True
questions.sourcecode:
class Chip:
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y

    def __eq__(self, other):
        return self.x == other.x and self.y == other.y


x1, y1 = map(int, input().split())
x2, y2 = map(int, input().split())
first = Chip(x1, y1)
second = Chip(x2, y2)
print(first == second)

Output Format:

questions.description:

Line 1: n
Next n lines: square <side> | rect <w> <h> | circle <r>

Output Format:
Line 1: str(combined) - names joined by + with the total area
Line 2: str(best) - the largest single shape

1 <= n <= 20; sides, widths, heights and radii are 1-100; circle area uses 3.14

Output Format:
The merged cart in first-occurrence order: <name> <price> <qty>

questions.title: Pluggable Report Exporters
questions.description:
A reporting service ships the same records through three duck-typed exporters - CsvExport, JsonExport and XmlExport - each exposing export(name, marks) with an identical interface and building its output text by hand (no json/csv/xml libraries).
Read the format code, pick the matching exporter object, then print every record through it.

Input Format:
Line 1: format code (csv, json or xml)
Line 2: n
Next n lines: name marks (names are single tokens)

Output Format:
csv: one line per record - name,marks
json: line {"students": [ , then two-space-indented {"name": "<n>", "marks": <m>} lines separated by commas (no comma after the last), then ]}
xml: line <students>, then <student name="<n>" marks="<m>"/> per record, then line </students>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 0 <= marks <= 100; names are single tokens
questions.sampleoutput1:
Ana,90
Bo,75
Cy,88
questions.output1:
<students>
<student name="Ravi" marks="60"/>
<student name="Sara" marks="95"/>
</students>
questions.output3: Zed,33
questions.inputconstrains: fmt is csv, json or xml; 1 <= n <= 50; 0 <= marks <= 100; names are single tokens
